product.name: llm-gateway
product.lede: llm-gateway is the serving side of llm: an authenticated HTTP gateway for one owner that relays the chat, responses and messages wires to the model targets its embedding hands out, and a hosting contract with a Runpod adapter for the pods those targets run on. It refuses before it guesses, publishes every refusal and bound, and translates no protocol. The shipped binary does not relay to a Runpod pod yet.
product.meta: Rust · one binary, one closed TOML document · specified in ESS · Apache-2.0

sections.title: One owner, a closed surface, nothing guessed.
sections.lede: Each property below is held by a named test in the repository gate.

items.title: One authenticated owner
items.description: Every route but the probes, the model listing and the setup page takes the owner's bearer credential, and an unauthenticated request cannot enumerate the surface.

items.title: Three wires, relayed byte for byte
items.description: Chat Completions, Responses and Messages reach the target unchanged but for the model name, and stream back as they arrive. A refused request never wakes a pod.

items.title: Client setup from the gateway itself
items.description: GET / answers the Codex, Claude Code or Loom settings for each model it serves, chosen by User-Agent, without a credential.

items.title: Relay to a Runpod pod from the binary
items.description: The Runpod pool and its connectors transport are tested against an emulator and a fixture; the binary refuses to use them until it reaches a pod over verified TLS.

sections.title: From the owner's POST to a relayed stream.
sections.lede: Each step refuses on its own, with a published code, before the next one runs.

steps.description: Probes first, then load shedding, then the public routes.

steps.label: owner
steps.title: Authenticate

tools.name: LLM
tools.description: The client side. llm-gateway answers llm's clients and reads Runpod's provider description from llm's providers crate at a release tag.

tools.name: Connectors
tools.description: The only way the Runpod transport reaches Runpod's control plane; it holds the Runpod API key.

tools.name: Loom
